title: Self-hosted SMTP relay (optional fallback)
description:
Simple SMTP server for receiving zkEmail verification emails.

## Purpose
Alternative to paste-email UX: users can send email TO Villa for DKIM extraction.

## Architecture
```
User sends email to verify@villa.cash
         ↓
SMTP Server (Postfix/Haraka)
         ↓
Extract DKIM headers only
         ↓
Return to client for ZK proof
         ↓
Discard email content immediately
```

## Implementation Options

### Option A: Haraka (Node.js)
- Easy to integrate with existing Node backend
- Plugin system for DKIM extraction
- Can run as Docker sidecar

### Option B: Postfix + Webhook
- Battle-tested MTA
- Forward to webhook on receipt
- More complex setup

## Docker Compose
```yaml
smtp-relay:
  image: haraka/haraka
  ports:
    - '25:25'
  environment:
    - DKIM_EXTRACT_ONLY=true
  volumes:
    - ./smtp-config:/etc/haraka
```

## Priority
P3 - Only needed if users prefer send-to over paste-email UX.
Can be added later without breaking existing flow.

title: OAuth integration (Google + Microsoft)
description:
Implement OAuth 2.0 for email verification with Google and Microsoft.

## Why OAuth?
- 1-click email verification (best UX)
- No email content access needed (only profile/email scope)
- Familiar flow for 90% of users

## Endpoints
- GET /api/auth/oauth/google - Initiate Google OAuth
- GET /api/auth/oauth/google/callback - Handle callback
- GET /api/auth/oauth/microsoft - Initiate Microsoft OAuth
- GET /api/auth/oauth/microsoft/callback - Handle callback
- DELETE /api/auth/oauth/[provider] - Disconnect OAuth

## Scopes Required
- Google: email, profile (read-only)
- Microsoft: User.Read, email (read-only)

## Flow
1. User clicks 'Continue with Google'
2. OAuth redirect → Google consent
3. Callback receives email
4. Hash email, store in email_verifications
5. Link to user's address

## Security
- State parameter for CSRF protection
- PKCE for mobile apps
- Never store email plaintext
- Encrypted token storage for refresh only

title: [Proposal] Evaluate Memvid for AI context management
description:
## Summary

Evaluate [Memvid](https://memvid.com/) as a context management layer for:
1. **Claude Code development context** (`.claude/` knowledge base)
2. **User agent context in TinyCloud** (user preferences, history)

## What is Memvid?

Memvid is a portable AI memory system that replaces vector databases with a single file. Two implementations exist:

| Version | Format | Embeddings | Features |
|---------|--------|------------|----------|
| [Python (original)](https://github.com/Olow304/memvid) | `.mp4` (QR codes in video) | SentenceTransformers + FAISS | 50-100x smaller than vector DBs |
| [Rust (new)](https://github.com/memvid/memvid) | `.mv2` (single file) | ONNX + HNSW | Sub-5ms retrieval, MCP server |

### Key Benefits
- **Single-file portable**: No database infrastructure needed
- **Offline-capable**: Works entirely locally after initial indexing
- **MCP integration**: [memvid_mcp_server](https://github.com/angrysky56/memvid_mcp_server) exposes tools to Claude
- **Sub-5ms search**: Fast semantic retrieval

## Can It Work With 500MB Local Qwen?

**⚠️ Critical misunderstanding to clarify:**

Memvid needs an **embedding model**, NOT a chat LLM. These are different:

| Model Type | Purpose | Example | Size |
|------------|---------|---------|------|
| **Chat LLM** | Generate text responses | Qwen-0.5B, Qwen-1.8B | 500MB-2GB |
| **Embedding Model** | Convert text → vectors | Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B | ~600MB |

### Embedding Options for Local Use

| Model | Size | Format | Notes |
|-------|------|--------|-------|
| [Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-ONNX](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-ONNX) | ~600MB (q8: ~300MB) | ONNX | Multilingual, 100+ languages |
| [all-MiniLM-L6-v2](https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) | ~90MB | PyTorch/ONNX | Smaller, English-focused |
| [Model2Vec distilled](https://huggingface.co/futur/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-model2vec-onnx) | <50MB | ONNX | 500x faster, lower quality |

**Answer:** Yes, but you need an embedding model alongside (or instead of) your chat LLM.

## Use Case Analysis

### 1. `.claude/` Development Context ✅ VIABLE

**What it could do:**
- Index all specs, learnings, reflections into one `.mv2` file
- Enable semantic search over project knowledge
- Persist context between sessions
- MCP server exposes tools for RAG-style queries

**Integration path:**
```
specs/ + .claude/LEARNINGS.md + reflections/
    ↓ (index once)
.claude/context.mv2 (single file)
    ↓ (MCP server)
Claude Code queries via tool calls
```

**Pros:**
- Better context retrieval than file search
- Survives compaction/session clears
- Single portable file

**Cons:**
- Adds complexity (embedding model + memvid runtime)
- Re-indexing needed when docs change
- MCP server is separate process to manage

### 2. TinyCloud User Agent Context ❌ MISALIGNED

**Why this doesn't fit:**

TinyCloud and Memvid solve different problems:

| Aspect | TinyCloud | Memvid |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| **Purpose** | Decentralized user data storage | AI memory/RAG |
| **Data** | Avatars, profiles, settings | Text chunks + embeddings |
| **Search** | Key-value lookup | Semantic similarity |
| **User-facing** | Yes | No (AI tool) |

**Current TinyCloud usage in Villa:**
- Custom avatar uploads (images)
- Cross-device profile sync

**What "user agent context" would need:**
- User preferences, chat history, behavioral patterns
- This is application state, not semantic memory
- Better served by database + simple key-value storage

**Recommendation:** Don't force Memvid into TinyCloud. They're orthogonal.

## Cost/Benefit Analysis

### For `.claude/` Context

| Factor | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| **Setup effort** | Medium (install embedding model, run MCP server) |
| **Maintenance** | Low (re-index on doc changes) |
| **Value** | Medium (better than grep, worse than Claude's native understanding) |
| **Risk** | Low (purely optional tooling) |

### For TinyCloud User Context

| Factor | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| **Setup effort** | High (would need custom integration layer) |
| **Maintenance** | High (sync issues, embedding drift) |
| **Value** | Low (overkill for user preferences) |
| **Risk** | Medium (adds complexity to user-facing path) |

## Recommendation

### Do: Experiment with `.claude/` context

1. Install memvid MCP server locally
2. Index `specs/` and `.claude/LEARNINGS.md`
3. Test retrieval quality over 1-2 weeks
4. If valuable, document as optional developer tool

### Don't: Integrate with TinyCloud

- TinyCloud is for user data (avatars, profiles)
- User "context" is better served by:
  - Session storage (ephemeral preferences)
  - Database (persistent preferences)
  - Browser localStorage (device-specific)

## Decision Points

**Before proceeding:**
1. Is semantic search over project docs actually a pain point?
2. Do we have the ~600MB budget for an embedding model?
3. Who maintains the MCP server process?
4. Is the value worth the complexity?

## Resources

- [Memvid Documentation](https://docs.memvid.com)
- [GitHub: memvid/memvid (Rust)](https://github.com/memvid/memvid)
- [GitHub: Olow304/memvid (Python)](https://github.com/Olow304/memvid)
- [Memvid MCP Server](https://github.com/angrysky56/memvid_mcp_server)
- [Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-ONNX](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-ONNX)
close_reason: Evaluated - ADR-002 written. Defer Memvid; current tooling sufficient for project scale

title: Recovery UI - Outstanding 2026 UX
description:
Create world-class recovery UI for email verification and account recovery.

## Design Principles
- 1-click where possible (OAuth)
- Clear visual hierarchy
- Mobile-first responsive
- Accessible (WCAG 2.1 AA)
- Micro-animations for delight

## Pages

### Email Linking (apps/key/src/app/email/page.tsx)
```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│  🔐 Add Recovery Email          │
│                                 │
│  Protect your Villa ID with an  │
│  email backup. Never lose       │
│  access to your account.        │
│                                 │
│  ┌─────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  G  Continue with Google │   │  ← Primary CTA
│  └─────────────────────────┘   │
│                                 │
│  ┌─────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  M  Continue with Microsoft│ │
│  └─────────────────────────┘   │
│                                 │
│  ─────────── or ───────────    │
│                                 │
│  🔒 Use Privacy Mode            │  ← zkEmail option
│  Verify without OAuth           │
│                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Account Recovery (apps/key/src/app/recovery/page.tsx)
```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│  🔑 Recover Your Villa ID       │
│                                 │
│  Lost your passkey? No problem. │
│  Sign in with your backup email.│
│                                 │
│  ┌─────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  G  Continue with Google │   │
│  └─────────────────────────┘   │
│                                 │
│  ┌─────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  M  Continue with Microsoft│ │
│  └─────────────────────────┘   │
│                                 │
│  🔒 Recover with Privacy Mode   │
│                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Settings Update (apps/key/src/app/settings/page.tsx)
- Show linked email domain (e.g., '****@gmail.com')
- 'Change recovery email' option
- 'Remove recovery email' with confirmation

### Auth Page Update (apps/key/src/app/auth/page.tsx)
- Add 'Recover with Email' link below passkey options
- Subtle but discoverable

## States
- idle → loading → success/error
- Skeleton loading for OAuth redirect
- Success confetti animation
- Error with clear retry action

## Accessibility
- Focus management
- Screen reader announcements
- Keyboard navigation
- High contrast support

title: zkEmail proof verification (privacy mode)
description:
Implement zkEmail verification for privacy-conscious users.

## Why zkEmail?
- No third-party OAuth dependency
- Email content never leaves user's device
- Cryptographic proof of ownership via DKIM
- Decentralized verification option

## Components

### Client-Side (SDK)
- packages/sdk/src/email/zkemail.ts
- Parse DKIM signature from raw email
- Generate ZK proof using @zk-email/helpers
- WASM-based proof generation in browser

### Server-Side
- POST /api/email/verify-zk - Verify zkEmail proof
- Validate proof against DKIM registry
- Store email hash on success

### UX Options
1. Paste raw email (export from inbox)
2. Send to verify@villa.cash (requires SMTP relay)

## Dependencies
- @zk-email/helpers ^3.0.0
- @zk-email/circuits ^3.0.0
- DKIM registry at registry.prove.email

title: [EPIC] zkEmail Recovery - Privacy-First Account Recovery for 2026
description:
## Epic: zkEmail + OAuth Recovery for Villa

### Vision
Best-in-class 2026 account recovery: OAuth for simplicity, zkEmail for privacy.

### Why Both?
- **OAuth (Google/Microsoft)**: 1-click email verification, familiar UX, 90% of users
- **zkEmail**: Privacy-preserving option for users who don't want OAuth, decentralized verification

### UX Flow
1. User clicks 'Link Email for Recovery'
2. Option A: 'Continue with Google/Microsoft' (OAuth - instant)
3. Option B: 'Use Privacy Mode' (zkEmail - paste email or send to verify@villa.cash)

### Key Principle
Email is for RECOVERY only, not primary auth. Passkeys remain the gold standard.

### Privacy Model
- OAuth: We only get email address, no access to inbox
- zkEmail: Zero-knowledge proof, email content never leaves device
- Both: Only keccak256(email) stored in DB, never plaintext

### Children Issues
1. EmailRecoverySignerV1 contract
2. Database schema for email verification
3. OAuth integration (Google + Microsoft)
4. zkEmail proof verification
5. SDK email methods
6. Recovery UI with outstanding UX
7. Self-hosted SMTP relay (optional fallback)
